Several distressing episodes a day at ten weeks cause real social withdrawal, and effective treatment is available now. (Source: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management)
source_refs: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management

options.rationale: Full antidepressant dosing over six weeks is the regimen for post stroke depression, which is not his diagnosis. Emotionalism responds at lower doses within days to a fortnight, so this over treats and delays the assessment of response. (Source: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management)
source_refs: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management

options.rationale: Stereotyped brief crying disproportionate to and dissociated from the underlying mood is post stroke emotionalism, and serotonergic antidepressants reduce episode frequency substantially. The response is typically evident within one to two weeks and at doses below those used for depression. (Source: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management)
source_refs: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management

options.rationale: Repeat imaging is warranted for new focal deficits or a change in conscious state, neither of which is present, and his examination is stable. Emotionalism after a supratentorial stroke is a recognised consequence rather than a sign of new infarction. (Source: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management)
source_refs: Stroke Foundation: Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management

explanation.summary: Behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia is the commonest cause of dementia under the age of sixty alongside Alzheimer disease and is routinely misdiagnosed as a primary psychiatric disorder for two to three years before the correct diagnosis is reached. The diagnostic criteria require three of six features: early behavioural disinhibition, apathy or inertia, loss of sympathy or empathy, perseverative or compulsive behaviour, hyperorality and dietary change, and a dysexecutive neuropsychological profile with relative sparing of memory and visuospatial function. The pattern of preserved orientation and recall alongside markedly reduced verbal fluency and perseveration is characteristic and is what a bedside screen such as a standardised cognitive test will miss, since those instruments are weighted towards memory. A family history is present in up to 40 per cent, with mutations in the C9orf72, MAPT and GRN genes accounting for most inherited cases. There is no disease modifying treatment, so the value of early diagnosis lies in behavioural management, carer support, decisions about work and driving, and access to younger onset dementia services and financial planning.
key_points: Personality and conduct change with preserved memory is the reverse of Alzheimer disease.
Disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, compulsions, hyperorality and dysexecutive testing.
Standard cognitive screens are insensitive because they weight memory and orientation.
A family history is present in up to 40 per cent of cases.
Cholinesterase inhibitors are ineffective and may worsen behaviour in this condition.
explanation.pearls: Verbal fluency is the single most useful bedside test when frontotemporal dementia is suspected: naming fewer than eleven animals in a minute is abnormal, and the discrepancy between a near normal memory score and a poor fluency score is what separates it from Alzheimer disease at first assessment.

options.rationale: Relationship intervention treats a psychosocial cause of behavioural change and carer strain is certainly present and worth supporting. Attributing an organic frontal syndrome to relationship difficulty places the responsibility on a man who cannot modify his behaviour. (Source: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines)

Mood stabilisation treats the mania that this presentation superficially resembles, which is why the referral was framed that way. Mania requires elevated or irritable mood with reduced sleep need and pressured speech, and the two year progressive course without any mood elevation excludes it. (Source: RANZCP: Mood disorders guideline)

Progressive disinhibition, loss of empathy, hyperorality and compulsive routines with preserved memory and orientation but impaired verbal fluency and perseveration is behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia. Imaging for frontal and anterior temporal atrophy plus neuropsychology is the diagnostic pathway. (Source: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines)

Reversible causes deserve exclusion in any new neuropsychiatric presentation and these tests are part of a standard workup. They do not account for a two year progressive frontal syndrome with a matching family history, and relying on them alone delays the diagnosis. (Source: RANZCP: Clinical practice guidelines)

Cholinesterase inhibitors are for Alzheimer disease, which presents with early episodic memory loss and preserved social conduct rather than the reverse pattern seen here. In frontotemporal dementia they are ineffective and can worsen behavioural symptoms. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

explanation.summary: Antidepressant associated hyponatraemia through the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis is a common and under recognised adverse effect, with the highest risk in the first two to four weeks of treatment and in people over 65, of low body weight, or taking diuretics. All selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors carry the risk and venlafaxine and mirtazapine carry it to a lesser degree. The biochemical diagnosis requires hypotonic hyponatraemia with a serum osmolality below 275 mmol/kg, an inappropriately concentrated urine above 100 mmol/kg, a urine sodium above 30 mmol/L, clinical euvolaemia, and the exclusion of hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency. Severity is driven by symptoms and by rate of fall rather than by the absolute number, and drowsiness, vomiting and confusion at 118 mmol/L constitute severe symptomatic hyponatraemia requiring inpatient management. The correction rate must not exceed 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours because of the risk of osmotic demyelination, and a baseline sodium should be checked before starting an antidepressant in an older person and repeated at two weeks.
key_points: Risk is highest in the first two to four weeks and in older, lighter, diuretic treated patients.
Diagnosis requires hypotonic hyponatraemia with concentrated urine and urine sodium above 30 mmol/L.
Exclude hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency before attributing it to the drug.
Saline can worsen the sodium in the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis.
Do not correct faster than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours because of osmotic demyelination risk.
explanation.pearls: Check a baseline sodium before starting an antidepressant in anyone over 65 and repeat it at two weeks, because the median time to symptomatic hyponatraemia is around 13 days and the presentation is usually non-specific confusion or a fall rather than anything that points to the electrolyte.

options.rationale: Euvolaemic hyponatraemia with a low serum osmolality, inappropriately concentrated urine and a urine sodium above 30 mmol/L is the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis, and the sertraline started three weeks ago is the new variable. Withdrawal of the drug with fluid restriction under inpatient monitoring is the correct combination at this sodium and conscious level. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Thiazide and thiazide like diuretics are a leading cause of hyponatraemia in older people and indapamide should certainly also be stopped, so half of this is right. It has been taken unchanged for six years while the sertraline is new, and saline in the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis can lower the sodium further. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

A fluid challenge is the right test when hypovolaemia is the suspected mechanism, but she has moist membranes, no postural drop and a urine sodium of 52 mmol/L, all of which indicate euvolaemia. Imaging investigates a structural cause for confusion that her electrolytes already explain. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Mirtazapine carries a lower risk of hyponatraemia and is a sensible choice when her depression is retreated later, so the drug selection itself is defensible. Substituting one antidepressant for another without treating a sodium of 118 mmol/L leaves the acute danger unaddressed. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Outpatient fluid restriction with repeat testing is reasonable for mild asymptomatic hyponatraemia in a well patient. A sodium of 118 mmol/L with drowsiness, disorientation and vomiting is severe symptomatic hyponatraemia and carries a risk of seizure and cerebral oedema. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

explanation.summary: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder is distinguished from ordinary premenstrual symptoms by the severity of the mood disturbance and by demonstrable impairment of work, study or relationships, and it is separated from an underlying mood or anxiety disorder by the presence of a genuinely symptom-free interval in the follicular phase. Because retrospective recall is unreliable and over attributes symptoms to the cycle, the diagnosis formally requires prospective daily ratings across at least two cycles, which is both a diagnostic step and a therapeutic one since many women find the pattern itself clarifying. The underlying mechanism is an abnormal central response to normal cyclical fluctuations in ovarian steroids and their neuroactive metabolites rather than any abnormality of hormone levels, which is why measuring hormones is unhelpful. Serotonergic antidepressants are first line and their rapid onset in this condition, quite unlike their three to four week latency in depression, permits continuous, luteal phase or symptom onset dosing. Second line options include a drospirenone containing combined oral contraceptive with a shortened hormone free interval, and ovarian suppression is reserved for severe refractory cases.
key_points: A symptom-free follicular interval separates this from an underlying mood disorder
Prospective daily ratings over two cycles are required for diagnosis
Hormone levels are normal and measuring them does not help
Serotonergic antidepressants act within days here, allowing luteal phase dosing
Luteal phase progesterone performs no better than placebo
explanation.pearls: Serotonergic antidepressants relieve premenstrual dysphoric disorder within 24 to 48 hours rather than the three to four weeks required in major depression, which is why dosing restricted to the 14 days before menstruation works and halves total drug exposure.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Pyridoxine has modest evidence for physical premenstrual symptoms at low dose but not for the mood syndrome, and doses above 100 mg daily carry a risk of peripheral sensory neuropathy with prolonged use. Evening primrose oil has not been shown to help. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

A drospirenone containing pill with a shortened hormone free interval is an effective second line option and is a reasonable choice for a woman who also wants contraception. It has a lower response rate than the serotonergic option and is not the first recommendation when contraception is not being sought. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Luteal phase progesterone has been studied repeatedly for this indication and performs no better than placebo. In some women it reproduces the very symptoms it is intended to treat. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Serotonergic antidepressants are the established first line treatment for this condition and are distinctive in that they work within a day or two rather than over weeks, which is what makes luteal phase only dosing a viable regimen. Roughly six in ten women respond. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

The cyclical pattern superficially resembles a rapid cycling mood disorder, which is why a mood stabiliser can seem logical, but her mood returns fully to baseline for two weeks of every cycle and is tied to the menstrual cycle rather than running autonomously. Lithium has no established role here. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: Expressed emotion describes the level of criticism, hostility and emotional overinvolvement directed toward a family member with a psychotic illness, and it is one of the most consistently replicated predictors of relapse, with relapse rates in high expressed emotion households roughly double those in low expressed emotion households over the year following discharge. The concept is not about blame: families arrive at these patterns through fear and exhaustion, and attributions such as laziness usually reflect a lack of information about negative symptoms rather than indifference. Structured family intervention combines psychoeducation about the illness and its treatment, communication skills training, structured problem solving and crisis planning, delivered over at least six months and generally around ten or more sessions. Meta analyses show reductions in relapse and readmission of about half, which places it among the most effective single interventions available in early psychosis and is why it is recommended for every family in contact with a first episode service. It works alongside maintenance antipsychotic medication, individual psychological therapy and vocational support rather than replacing any of them.
key_points: High expressed emotion roughly doubles relapse rates over the first year
Criticism, hostility and emotional overinvolvement are the three components
Attributions such as laziness usually reflect misunderstanding of negative symptoms
Structured family intervention runs over at least six months and around ten sessions
Relapse and readmission fall by approximately half
explanation.pearls: Ask a carer what they think causes the person's inactivity: an answer framed as a character flaw rather than an illness feature identifies high expressed emotion at the bedside and predicts relapse more reliably than any symptom rating scale.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
Orygen Youth Health Clinical Practice Guidelines

options.rationale: Individual placement and support improves vocational outcomes and is an important part of early psychosis care, but its demonstrated effect is on employment rather than on relapse. It sits alongside rather than ahead of the family work. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: He has already responded well at the current dose and is taking it reliably, so there is no pharmacological failure to correct. Raising the dose adds metabolic and extrapyramidal burden, which is itself a common reason young people stop medication and relapse. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Antidepressants have a limited and inconsistent effect on negative symptoms, and no depressive syndrome has been described here. Adding a second psychotropic without a clear indication complicates the regimen. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Individual cognitive behavioural therapy for psychosis is recommended and helps residual symptoms and distress, so this is a genuine component of good care rather than a wrong treatment. It does not address the household environment, which is the specific modifiable factor operating here. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Households with high levels of criticism, hostility or emotional overinvolvement carry a substantially higher relapse rate, and the pattern described in this meeting fits both the critical and the overinvolved forms. Structured family work delivered over several months reduces relapse and readmission by roughly half, an effect size comparable to maintenance medication. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Australian mental health legislation has moved from a substitute decision making model toward supported decision making, reflecting obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. The practical instruments that express this are the advance statement of preferences, made while the person has capacity and setting out the treatment they would and would not want in a future episode, and the nominated support person, who is appointed to help the person express their own will and preferences rather than to decide on their behalf. Treating teams must consider an advance statement and, in most jurisdictions, must record written reasons if compulsory treatment departs from it, which means the document shapes clinical decisions even though it does not bind them absolutely. The clinical value extends beyond the legal effect: the conversation itself identifies which aspects of previous admissions the person found most distressing, such as seclusion, a particular medication or the involvement of police, and often surfaces workable alternatives. Recovery oriented practice treats episodes of incapacity as interruptions in an ongoing relationship with an autonomous person rather than as a licence to disregard their preferences.
key_points: Advance statements are made while capacity is retained for use during later incapacity
Teams must consider the statement and usually give written reasons for departing from it
A nominated support person assists expression of the person's own preferences
Compulsory orders require the statutory criteria to be met at the time, not in advance
The planning conversation surfaces workable alternatives to distressing past interventions
explanation.pearls: Ask specifically which part of a previous admission the person found most distressing and what helped: answers such as a preference for olanzapine over haloperidol, or for a particular relative to be called before police, are exactly what an advance statement can make binding on the team's reasoning.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
Mental Health Act frameworks for Australian states and territories

options.rationale: An advance statement is made while a person has capacity and records the treatment they would want, and would not want, if they later become unwell and lose it. Australian mental health legislation requires treating teams to consider such a statement and to give written reasons when they depart from it, so completing it now is the action that gives her genuine influence over future episodes. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: A compulsory order can only be made when the statutory criteria are met at the time, which requires a current mental illness with the person unable to consent and a risk that cannot be addressed less restrictively. She is well and consenting, and a pre-emptive order is not lawful. (Source: Mental Health Act frameworks for Australian states and territories)
source_refs: Mental Health Act frameworks for Australian states and territories

options.rationale: Guardianship transfers decision making away from the person and is reserved for those with enduring incapacity, usually from cognitive impairment or disability. Her incapacity is episodic and she currently has capacity, so this is a disproportionate response that achieves the opposite of what she is asking for. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: A file note carries no standing under mental health legislation and may not be found by a team meeting her in an emergency. The statutory instrument exists precisely so that her wishes carry weight rather than depending on whether someone reads the notes. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Nominating a support person is a legitimate and valuable part of this planning, but a nominated person supports the individual to express their own will and preferences rather than substituting their judgement. Handing the decision to family bypasses her stated wishes. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Trichotillomania is classified among the obsessive compulsive and related disorders and is defined by recurrent pulling of one's own hair resulting in hair loss, with repeated attempts to stop and associated distress or impairment. Onset is typically in early adolescence and it is considerably more common in females presenting to clinics. Pulling occurs in two modes that often coexist: a focused mode preceded by mounting tension and followed by relief or gratification, and an automatic mode occurring outside awareness during sedentary activities such as reading or screen time, which is why awareness training is a necessary first component of treatment. The distinction from alopecia areata rests on the appearance of the patches, since mechanical pulling leaves hairs broken at varying lengths within an irregularly shaped area of otherwise normal scalp, whereas areata produces smooth complete loss with tapered exclamation mark hairs. Trichophagia should be asked about directly because swallowed hair can form a gastric trichobezoar with a tail extending into the small bowel, a rare but surgically important complication.
key_points: Broken hairs of varying lengths in an irregular patch indicate pulling, not alopecia areata
Pulling occurs in both focused and automatic modes, often in the same person
Habit reversal training is first line and outperforms medication
Serotonergic antidepressants have largely negative trial evidence for this condition
Ask directly about swallowing hair because of the risk of a gastric trichobezoar
explanation.pearls: Always ask whether the person swallows the hair they pull, because a trichobezoar with a tail extending through the pylorus into the jejunum presents with vomiting and weight loss and requires surgical removal rather than any psychiatric treatment.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Serotonergic antidepressants are effective for obsessive compulsive disorder itself but trials in hair pulling have been largely negative, which is one of the features that separates this condition from obsessive compulsive disorder despite their grouping together. It may still be used where a comorbid depressive or anxiety disorder is present. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Behavioural treatment combining awareness training, a competing response and stimulus control has the strongest evidence for this condition and is recommended ahead of medication. Awareness training matters particularly here because much of her pulling is automatic and outside her attention. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

N acetylcysteine has some supportive trial evidence in adults and is reasonably well tolerated, which makes it a recognised second line option. The evidence in adolescents is weaker and it is not used ahead of the behavioural treatment. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Topical corticosteroid treats alopecia areata, which is the diagnosis she was originally given, and the two are separated by the examination findings. Areata produces smooth complete bald patches with tapered exclamation mark hairs, whereas broken hairs of differing lengths within an irregular patch indicate mechanical extraction. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Antipsychotic augmentation has been trialled in refractory cases but carries substantial metabolic risk in an adolescent. It is not a first line treatment for a condition with an effective and well tolerated behavioural option. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: Trans and gender diverse young people have substantially higher rates of depression, anxiety, self-harm and suicidal ideation than their peers, and the evidence indicates that this excess is driven predominantly by external factors including bullying, family rejection, misgendering and barriers to care rather than by gender identity itself. Family support and the ability to use one's name and pronouns are among the strongest protective factors identified. The Australian standards of care set out a multidisciplinary model in which assessment covers gender identity and its development, mental health, family and social circumstances, and fertility considerations, and in which psychological support, social affirmation, medical options and advocacy in school settings all sit within the same plan. Mental health treatment proceeds in parallel rather than as a prerequisite, because delaying access while waiting for symptoms to remit both prolongs distress and is associated with disengagement. Practices aimed at changing or suppressing gender identity are ineffective, are linked to worse outcomes and are unlawful in several Australian jurisdictions.
key_points: Excess mental illness in this group is driven largely by external stressors, not identity
Family support and correct name and pronoun use are strong protective factors
Assessment for those under 18 is multidisciplinary and includes fertility discussion
Treat mental health concerns in parallel rather than as a prerequisite to referral
Practices aimed at changing gender identity are ineffective and unlawful in several jurisdictions
explanation.pearls: Consistent use of a young person's chosen name across home, school and health settings is associated with a substantial reduction in depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation, which makes documenting the name and pronouns in the medical record a clinical intervention rather than an administrative one.

sources.label: Royal Children's Hospital Australian Standards of Care for Trans and Gender Diverse Children and Adolescents
Australian Professional Association for Trans Health
Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Gender affirming hormone therapy in a person under 18 follows assessment by an experienced multidisciplinary team, with consideration of fertility preservation and the relevant consent framework. Initiating it at a first general practice visit bypasses each of those steps. (Source: Australian Professional Association for Trans Health)
source_refs: Australian Professional Association for Trans Health

options.rationale: Sequencing care this way is intuitive because clinicians reasonably want a clear assessment, but the distress here is substantially driven by the very issues being deferred, so the depression is unlikely to lift while they remain unaddressed. Deferral is itself experienced as a barrier and is associated with disengagement from care. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Australian Standards of Care for Trans and Gender Diverse Children and Adolescents)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Australian Standards of Care for Trans and Gender Diverse Children and Adolescents

options.rationale: Assessment for gender related medical care in a person under 18 is undertaken by a multidisciplinary service, and referral should not wait for mental health difficulties to resolve because the distress is closely tied to the unresolved gender related concerns and to the bullying. Treating the depressive symptoms concurrently with psychological therapy and school advocacy addresses both strands at once. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Australian Standards of Care for Trans and Gender Diverse Children and Adolescents)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Australian Standards of Care for Trans and Gender Diverse Children and Adolescents

options.rationale: Australian practice provides for assessment and, where appropriate, treatment of people under 18 through specialist services, and turning 18 is not a legal or clinical threshold for beginning assessment. A blanket deferral leaves the current distress untreated. (Source: Australian Professional Association for Trans Health)
source_refs: Australian Professional Association for Trans Health

options.rationale: Therapy directed at changing or discouraging a person's gender identity is ineffective, is associated with worse mental health outcomes, and is prohibited by legislation in several Australian jurisdictions. Exploratory psychological support is part of specialist assessment, but it is not framed as testing whether the identity is genuine. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Corticosteroid induced psychiatric disturbance is strongly dose dependent, with risk rising sharply above the equivalent of about 40 mg of prednisolone daily and reaching close to one in five patients at doses above 80 mg. Onset is usually within the first two weeks of starting or increasing the dose. The presentation is more often elevated or mixed than depressive in the acute phase, while depressive syndromes are more characteristic of long term therapy and of the withdrawal period, and a hypoactive delirium can also occur, particularly in older patients. Importantly, a personal or family history of psychiatric illness is not a reliable predictor, so the absence of one offers no reassurance, whereas a previous episode on corticosteroid strongly predicts recurrence. Management prioritises reducing the dose to the minimum required for the underlying disease, which usually resolves the syndrome within days to weeks, with an antipsychotic used for symptom control in the interim and abrupt cessation avoided because of adrenal suppression.
key_points: Risk rises steeply above about 40 mg prednisolone equivalent daily
Onset is typically within the first two weeks of starting or increasing the dose
Elevated and mixed states predominate acutely, depression with chronic use and withdrawal
A negative psychiatric history does not predict who will be affected
Reduce the dose in negotiation with the treating team and never stop abruptly
explanation.pearls: A previous corticosteroid induced psychiatric episode is the single strongest predictor of another, so document it prominently and consider prophylactic olanzapine or lithium cover if a future high dose course above 40 mg prednisolone equivalent becomes necessary.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Corticosteroids can produce depressive as well as elevated states, and an antidepressant would be considered for the former. Giving one during an elevated episode risks worsening it. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Stopping abruptly after eleven days of high dose therapy risks adrenal insufficiency and would allow the lung disease to flare, which is a worse outcome than the psychiatric syndrome being treated. Corticosteroids are reduced in a planned way, not stopped outright. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Lithium has been used prophylactically in patients requiring repeated corticosteroid courses, which gives this option some basis, but it has a slow onset, a narrow therapeutic index and requires stable fluid balance and renal function in an acutely unwell inpatient. It is not the treatment for an episode that is already established. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

The disturbance is dose related, so reducing the corticosteroid to the lowest dose that controls the lung disease is the definitive step and must be negotiated with the treating team rather than decided unilaterally. An antipsychotic provides symptom control in the interim, and olanzapine has the best evidence in this setting. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

He is making financial commitments he cannot meet and has had four nights of severe sleep disruption, which represents active risk rather than a syndrome that can be observed. Waiting a week allows further irreversible decisions. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Narcolepsy type 1 arises from loss of hypothalamic orexin producing neurons, most likely through an autoimmune mechanism, and typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood, yet diagnostic delay commonly exceeds a decade and misdiagnosis as depression is among the commonest reasons, because both present with a young person who is sleepy, withdrawn and underperforming. Cataplexy is the near specific feature and consists of brief bilateral loss of muscle tone triggered by strong emotion, most often laughter, with consciousness fully preserved, and it must be asked about directly because patients rarely volunteer it and often describe it only as weakness or as knees giving way. The remaining features are sleep paralysis, hypnagogic hallucinations and disrupted nocturnal sleep. Narcolepsy is separated from depressive hypersomnia by the quality of sleep and naps: in narcolepsy naps are brief and genuinely restorative and night sleep is not extended, whereas depressive hypersomnia produces long unrefreshing sleep, difficulty getting out of bed and naps that leave the person no better. Diagnosis rests on overnight polysomnography excluding other causes followed by a multiple sleep latency test the next day.
key_points: Cataplexy is brief emotion triggered bilateral tone loss with preserved consciousness
Patients rarely volunteer cataplexy, so ask directly about weakness when laughing
Refreshing brief naps distinguish narcolepsy from depressive hypersomnia
Antidepressant trials leave the sleepiness unchanged
Polysomnography followed by a multiple sleep latency test is the diagnostic standard
explanation.pearls: Ask every sleepy young patient what happens to their body when they laugh hard: a description of jaw slackening, head nodding or knees buckling for a few seconds with full awareness is cataplexy and shifts the diagnosis from depression to narcolepsy in a single question.

sources.label: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

options.rationale: Oximetry screens for obstructive sleep apnoea, the other major cause of excessive daytime sleepiness, and would be sensible if his history suggested it. He has a normal body mass index, no snoring, no witnessed apnoeas and describes naps as refreshing, whereas sleepiness from apnoea is characteristically unrefreshed. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association)

Two adequate trials have already left the sleepiness untouched, and the features that would support a depressive hypersomnia are absent since he retains interest and wakes refreshed. A third trial repeats a strategy that has already failed for the dominant symptom. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Screening for metabolic and haematological causes of fatigue is a reasonable general step and thyroid function and ferritin have already returned within normal limits. None of these tests explains the episodes of emotionally triggered weakness, which is the discriminating feature. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association)

Imaging is indicated when a secondary cause is suspected, such as a hypothalamic or pineal region lesion, signalled by focal neurological signs, headache, visual change or endocrine disturbance. He has none of these and the yield in a typical presentation is very low. (Source: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists)
source_refs: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

options.rationale: Brief bilateral loss of muscle tone triggered by strong emotion, together with refreshing naps and preserved interest, points to a primary disorder of sleep and wake regulation rather than to depression. Overnight study followed the next day by a multiple sleep latency test is the diagnostic standard, demonstrating a short mean sleep latency with early entry into rapid eye movement sleep. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association)

explanation.summary: Akathisia is a subjective sense of inner restlessness accompanied by an inability to remain still, and it is among the most distressing adverse effects of antipsychotic medication. It is most common in the first weeks after starting or increasing a drug, and aripiprazole is notable for causing it despite otherwise favourable extrapyramidal tolerability. The central clinical danger is misattribution: the outward picture of a pacing, unsettled patient is easily recorded as agitation or as worsening psychosis, which leads to dose escalation or additional as needed antipsychotic and a worsening cycle, and a documented deterioration after each as needed dose is the pattern that should prompt reconsideration. Restless legs syndrome is the main differential and is separated by the localisation of the urge to the legs, the circadian worsening in the evening and at rest, relief with movement, and an association with low ferritin. Management is reduction of the causative dose or a switch to an agent with lower liability, with propranolol as the best supported symptomatic treatment and benzodiazepines or mirtazapine as alternatives, while anticholinergics are ineffective.
key_points: Akathisia combines subjective inner restlessness with observable motor restlessness
It appears within weeks of starting or increasing an antipsychotic
Misreading it as agitation leads to dose escalation and a worsening cycle
Anticholinergics treat parkinsonism and dystonia but not akathisia
Restless legs is localised to the legs, worse at rest in the evening, and linked to low ferritin
explanation.pearls: A patient who becomes more unsettled after each as needed dose of antipsychotic has akathisia rather than agitation, and propranolol 10 to 20 mg three times daily alongside dose reduction is the response, not another dose of the drug causing it.

options.rationale: Subjective inner restlessness with observable motor restlessness beginning within weeks of an antipsychotic change is drug induced akathisia, and dose reduction addresses the cause while a lipophilic beta blocker is the best supported symptomatic treatment. Recognising it matters because akathisia is associated with increased suicide risk and with treatment discontinuation. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

This is the error the ward has already made twice, and the record that he worsened after each as needed dose is the clue. Treating akathisia as psychotic agitation escalates the very drug causing it and produces a cycle of increasing dose and increasing distress. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Anticholinergic agents are effective for drug induced parkinsonism and acute dystonia but perform poorly for akathisia, which is the extrapyramidal syndrome they do not treat. He has neither tremor nor cogwheel rigidity to suggest parkinsonism. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Dopamine agonists treat restless legs syndrome, in which the urge is localised to the legs, is worst in the evening and at rest, and is relieved by movement. His restlessness is generalised and constant throughout the day, his ferritin is not low, and a dopamine agonist risks aggravating psychosis. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association)

Iron deficiency drives restless legs syndrome and replacement is indicated when ferritin falls below about 75 micrograms/L. His ferritin is well above that threshold, so there is no deficiency to correct. (Source: Australasian Sleep Association)

explanation.summary: Drug induced QT prolongation results from blockade of the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current, and risk accumulates additively across contributing factors rather than resting on any single one. The relevant factors here are two QT prolonging drugs taken together, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, bradycardia and female sex, which independently confers a longer baseline interval. Absolute thresholds matter for action: an interval above 500 milliseconds, or an increase of more than 60 milliseconds from baseline, marks a substantially increased risk of torsades de pointes, and this patient meets both criteria. Citalopram carries a specific dose-dependent warning, with maximum recommended doses of 40 mg in adults and 20 mg in those over 60 or with hepatic impairment. Immediate management corrects the reversible physiological contributors, which means replacing potassium to the upper half of the reference range and giving magnesium even when only mildly low, with continuous monitoring, while rationalisation of the psychotropic regimen follows once the acute risk is controlled.
key_points: Risk accumulates additively across drugs, electrolytes, bradycardia and sex
An interval above 500 milliseconds or a rise above 60 milliseconds from baseline is the action threshold
Replace magnesium even when only mildly low because it stabilises the myocardium
Citalopram prolongs the interval in a dose-dependent way with a specific maximum dose warning
Correct the reversible physiology first, then rationalise the psychotropic regimen
explanation.pearls: Replace potassium to the upper half of the reference range rather than merely into it when the corrected QT exceeds 500 milliseconds, and give magnesium regardless of a borderline level, because serum magnesium correlates poorly with total body stores.

options.rationale: An interval above 500 milliseconds with ongoing electrolyte depletion and bradycardia represents a present risk of a malignant arrhythmia rather than a trend to observe. A week of unchanged treatment leaves every contributing factor in place. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular)

Hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia are the fastest reversible contributors to the prolonged interval and both must be corrected promptly, with magnesium replaced even when the level is only modestly low because it stabilises the myocardium. Continuous monitoring is required at this interval because the risk of torsades de pointes rises steeply beyond 500 milliseconds. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular)

Both drugs prolong the interval and their effects are additive, and citalopram is specifically dose dependent in this respect with 40 mg exceeding the maximum recommended dose for patients over 60 and carrying a regulatory warning at any age. Stopping only one leaves a substantial pharmacological contribution untreated. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Magnesium is certainly the treatment once the arrhythmia has begun, which is why this option feels familiar, but withholding it until then forgoes the opportunity to prevent an event that can be fatal on first occurrence. Prophylactic correction of a documented deficiency is standard. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular)

A switch to a lower risk agent will form part of the plan, but choosing and titrating a new antipsychotic is a decision for the coming days rather than the immediate response. It does nothing about the electrolytes or the bradycardia, which are the acute drivers. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: Huntington disease is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by an expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat in the HTT gene, with full penetrance at 40 or more repeats and anticipation through paternal transmission. Psychiatric and behavioural change frequently precedes the movement disorder by years, and irritability, apathy, disinhibition and depression are the usual presentations, which is why these patients often reach a psychiatric service first and accumulate several failed antidepressant trials. The motor signs to seek deliberately are chorea, often absorbed into apparently purposeful gestures early on, motor impersistence demonstrated by inability to sustain tongue protrusion or a steady grip, and slowed or delayed initiation of saccades, which is one of the earliest reliable findings. A family history may be obscured, since a parent who died young of another cause, or whose illness was labelled as early dementia, alcoholism or a psychiatric disorder, is common. Testing is performed through a genetic service because the result determines risk for children and siblings who have not asked to know, and because suicide risk around the time of diagnosis is elevated.
key_points: Psychiatric and behavioural change often precedes chorea by several years
Motor impersistence and slowed saccades are early and easily missed signs
Chorea is initially incorporated into voluntary movements and looks like fidgeting
A parent labelled with early dementia or alcoholism may represent an obscured family history
Genetic testing proceeds through a counselling framework because relatives are implicated
explanation.pearls: Ask the patient to protrude the tongue and hold it out for ten seconds, and to grip your fingers steadily: inability to sustain either, known as motor impersistence, appears early in Huntington disease and is often present before chorea is obvious enough to be noticed by the family.

sources.label: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

options.rationale: Two adequate trials have failed and the presentation includes a progressive movement disorder and executive change that no antidepressant explains. Further sequential trials are the mechanism by which this diagnosis is typically delayed for years. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

The test itself is the right test, which is what makes this tempting, but delivering a result of this kind without pre test counselling, assessment of the patient's understanding, and planning for how at risk relatives will be informed is contrary to established practice. Each of his children carries a one in two prior risk and their position must be considered before the result exists. (Source: Human Genetics Society of Australasia)

Progressive personality change with apathy and disinhibition, chorea with motor impersistence and slowed saccades, and a parent who died young with a psychiatric and cognitive illness together indicate an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder. Testing for it carries profound implications for the patient, his children and his insurance and employment, so it is performed within a genetic counselling framework rather than ordered from a psychiatric clinic. (Source: Human Genetics Society of Australasia)

Dopamine blocking agents including tetrabenazine are used for functionally disabling chorea later in the illness, so this is a treatment on the right pathway at the wrong time. Starting one before the diagnosis is established obscures the movement disorder and risks it being reattributed to the drug. (Source: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists)
source_refs: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

options.rationale: Imaging may show caudate atrophy with enlarged frontal horns but this appears relatively late and a normal scan would not exclude the diagnosis. It is a supportive investigation rather than the step that resolves the question. (Source: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists)
source_refs: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

explanation.summary: The relationship between isotretinoin and depression has been debated for three decades and the population level evidence does not establish causation, with large cohort and case crossover studies showing no increase in depression or suicide attributable to the drug, and several suggesting that mood improves as severe acne clears. Severe acne is itself independently associated with depression, social withdrawal and suicidal ideation, which confounds the comparison substantially. Despite this, both Australian product information and prescribing practice require that patients and families be counselled about mood change before starting, that mood be reviewed at each visit, and that the drug be ceased if significant psychiatric symptoms emerge, reflecting the asymmetry between a reversible pause in an elective treatment and the consequences of a missed adolescent depression. In practice the two are held together: the population evidence determines whether the drug is reasonable to prescribe, while the individual presentation determines what to do next for this patient. Any adolescent expressing thoughts that others would be better off without them requires assessment within days regardless of what medication they are taking.
key_points: Population evidence does not establish a causal link with depression or suicide
Severe acne independently carries a substantial risk of depression, confounding the association
Product information nonetheless directs cessation if significant mood change emerges
Population level evidence governs prescribing, not the response to an individual event
Passive death wishes in an adolescent require assessment within days
explanation.pearls: Counsel about mood and ask about it at every isotretinoin review, and record the conversation, because the obligation to monitor and to cease on significant mood change holds under Australian product information regardless of what the epidemiological evidence shows about causation.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: A dose relationship has not been established for the psychiatric association, so halving the dose has no evidential basis for resolving the problem. It preserves the exposure while delaying definitive action. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Adding a second medication while continuing a drug that requires cessation under its own product information leaves the possible contributor in place and complicates the picture. It also delays the specialist assessment that his suicidal thinking warrants. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

A four week interval is far too long for an adolescent who has expressed thoughts that others would be better off without him. Passive death wishes require assessment within days, not weeks. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Whatever the strength of the causal evidence at population level, the product information directs cessation if significant mood change or suicidal ideation emerges, and the presence of active passive death wishes in an adolescent with a previous depressive episode makes continuing the drug indefensible. Stopping is reversible and the acne can be reconsidered once he is well. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

It is correct that large cohort studies have not established causation and that severe acne itself carries a substantial risk of depression, so the reasoning behind this option is genuinely sound at population level. That evidence governs whether the drug should be prescribed at all, not what to do for the individual in front of you who has developed suicidal thinking while taking it. (Source: Australasian College of Dermatologists)

explanation.summary: Wilson disease is an autosomal recessive disorder of the ATP7B copper transporter, causing failure of biliary copper excretion and of copper incorporation into caeruloplasmin, with accumulation in liver, brain, cornea and kidney, and although it is fatal untreated it is treatable, which is why it must be actively excluded in any patient under about 50 presenting with an unexplained movement disorder, unexplained liver disease, or a psychiatric presentation accompanied by either. Psychiatric features are the presenting complaint in around a third and include personality change, disinhibition, mood disturbance and occasionally psychosis, and they characteristically precede the neurological signs. Two findings in this case should redirect the assessment: markedly disproportionate sensitivity to a low dose of a dopamine blocking drug, which reflects pre-existing basal ganglia injury, and mildly deranged transaminases with a normal bilirubin in a young person. The critical diagnostic pitfall is the caeruloplasmin: it is normal in roughly one in ten patients overall and more often in those with active inflammation, so a value within the reference range must never be used to close the question. Basal 24 hour urinary copper excretion above 1.6 micromol per day supports the diagnosis and slit lamp examination for Kayser Fleischer rings is positive in almost all neurological cases.
key_points: Exclude Wilson disease in anyone under 50 with unexplained movement or liver disease
Psychiatric features precede neurological signs in a substantial proportion
Severe extrapyramidal reaction to a low antipsychotic dose is a warning sign
A caeruloplasmin within the reference range does not exclude the diagnosis
Basal 24 hour urinary copper with slit lamp examination establishes most neurological cases
explanation.pearls: Kayser Fleischer rings are present in over 95 per cent of patients with neurological Wilson disease but in only about half of those presenting with liver disease alone, so a slit lamp examination is close to definitive in exactly the group that reaches a psychiatric or neurology clinic.

sources.label: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

options.rationale: This treats a result at the very bottom of the reference range as though it excludes the diagnosis. Caeruloplasmin is an acute phase reactant that rises with inflammation, oestrogen and pregnancy, and it sits within the reference range in a meaningful minority of affected patients, so a normal value never excludes the condition and repeating it answers nothing. (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia)

Imaging may show characteristic changes in the basal ganglia and midbrain and is part of the assessment once the diagnosis is being pursued. The appearances are supportive rather than diagnostic and would not distinguish this from other causes of a young onset movement disorder. (Source: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists)
source_refs: Australian and New Zealand Association of Neurologists

options.rationale: Total serum copper is misleading because most circulating copper is bound to caeruloplasmin, so the total falls in parallel with the carrier protein and can appear low, normal or high depending on the balance between reduced carrier and increased free copper. It is not used as a diagnostic test. (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia)

Hepatic copper quantification remains the reference standard and retains a role when non-invasive testing is equivocal, which makes it the strongest competing answer. It is invasive, carries bleeding risk, and is not the appropriate first step when a urine collection and a slit lamp examination will resolve the question in most neurological presentations. (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia)

Basal 24 hour urinary copper excretion is the most useful screening test when the diagnosis is suspected in a symptomatic patient and is raised in almost all those with neurological presentations, which is exactly the group this man falls into. Combined with slit lamp examination for corneal rings, which are present in nearly every patient with neurological involvement, it establishes the diagnosis in most cases without invasive testing. (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia)

explanation.summary: Chronic tic disorder and Tourette disorder are diagnosed clinically from motor and vocal tics persisting beyond a year with onset before age eighteen, and no investigation is required when the examination is otherwise normal. Severity typically peaks between ten and twelve years and then declines through adolescence, so a large part of management is explaining the natural history to the family and the school. Treatment is driven by functional impact rather than by tic count, and a child who is coping needs education and school liaison rather than therapy. Comorbid attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and obsessive compulsive disorder are present in roughly half of referred children and often cause more impairment than the tics themselves, so they are screened for at every visit. Medication is added only when behavioural treatment has failed or is not accessible.
key_points: Tics that wax, wane and migrate with a premonitory urge and suppressibility are typical rather than concerning
Treat on functional impairment, not on how many tics are counted in a consultation
Habit reversal based behavioural therapy is the first line treatment for impairing tics
Screen every child with tics for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and obsessive compulsive symptoms
Antipsychotics are second line and require weight and metabolic monitoring
explanation.pearls: The premonitory urge is the therapeutic handle: children old enough to describe that build up of tension, usually from about nine years, are the ones who can be taught a competing response, and eight to ten weekly sessions is the standard course.

sources.label: American Academy of Neurology: Treatment of Tics

options.rationale: Watchful waiting with psychoeducation is right when tics are noticed but not causing distress or functional loss, which is not the case once a child is avoiding the playground and eating lunch alone. Deferring for a year leaves an impairing symptom untreated through a full school year. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Behavioural therapy built on habit reversal, in which the child learns to recognise the premonitory urge and perform a competing response, is the recommended first treatment for impairing tics and outperforms watchful waiting without drug adverse effects. The premonitory urge he describes is what makes him a good candidate, since the technique depends on being able to feel the tic coming. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Dopamine blocking agents do reduce tic severity but carry weight gain, sedation and extrapyramidal risk, so they sit behind behavioural therapy and are reserved for tics that remain disabling after it has been tried or is unavailable. Risperidone differs from clonidine in acting on the dopaminergic rather than the noradrenergic limb, which is why its adverse effect profile is metabolic rather than cardiovascular. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Clonidine is a reasonable pharmacological choice when tics coexist with prominent inattention or hyperactivity, neither of which his teacher describes, and it still ranks behind behavioural therapy as an opening move. It would be correct if a drug were needed and there were comorbid attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. (Source: American Academy of Neurology: Treatment of Tics)
source_refs: American Academy of Neurology: Treatment of Tics

options.rationale: Aripiprazole has the best evidence among the antipsychotics for tic reduction in children, but the same sequencing argument applies and behavioural therapy has not yet been offered. Starting it now exposes him to appetite and metabolic monitoring for a symptom that may respond to a time limited course of therapy. (Source: American Academy of Neurology: Treatment of Tics)
source_refs: American Academy of Neurology: Treatment of Tics

explanation.summary: Dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin release from the anterior pituitary, so any drug that blocks the D2 receptor releases that brake and raises prolactin. The degree of rise tracks the degree of blockade, which is why risperidone, paliperidone and amisulpride are the usual culprits while aripiprazole, quetiapine and clozapine are comparatively sparing. Sustained hyperprolactinaemia matters beyond the visible symptoms because the resulting hypogonadism reduces bone mineral density over years. The key interpretive step is the magnitude of the level: drug induced elevations usually sit below about 2000 mIU/L, whereas a macroprolactinoma generally drives prolactin far higher and comes with mass effect symptoms. Baseline prolactin before starting an antipsychotic makes this distinction much easier later.
key_points: Check a pregnancy test and thyroid function before attributing galactorrhoea to a drug
Risperidone, paliperidone and amisulpride are the high prolactin antipsychotics
Aripiprazole is a partial dopamine agonist and typically lowers prolactin toward normal
Image the pituitary only for very high levels, mass effect symptoms, or persistence after the drug is stopped
Untreated hyperprolactinaemic hypogonadism costs bone density over the long term
explanation.pearls: Aripiprazole reduces antipsychotic induced prolactin within about four weeks and can be used as a low dose adjunct of 5 to 10 mg daily when the original agent must be kept for efficacy reasons.

options.rationale: Imaging is indicated when prolactin rises above roughly 2000 to 3000 mIU/L, when there is headache or visual field loss, or when the elevation persists after the offending drug is withdrawn, none of which applies here. Scanning first risks finding an incidental microadenoma and anchoring management on it. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Risperidone and amisulpride raise prolactin most among the second generation agents, and switching to a partial dopamine agonist normalises prolactin in most patients within weeks while maintaining antipsychotic cover. This preserves the treatment she wants to continue rather than trading her remission for her cycle. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

A dopamine agonist can lower prolactin but is working directly against the antipsychotic at the receptor it blocks, and carries a real risk of destabilising the psychosis. Cabergoline is the right drug for a true prolactinoma, which is the distinction from the drug induced picture here. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Inducing a withdrawal bleed masks the hormonal abnormality without addressing the dopamine blockade that is driving it, and the galactorrhoea will persist. Oestrogen replacement has a place only when the causative drug genuinely cannot be changed and bone protection is the aim. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Stopping treatment eight months after a first episode carries a high relapse risk and is not justified by a reversible endocrine adverse effect with an easy pharmacological solution. Guidance supports continuing an antipsychotic for at least one to two years after a first episode. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: Lithium associated nephrogenic diabetes insipidus affects a substantial minority of long term users and is dose and duration dependent rather than a sign of toxicity, which is why it appears at therapeutic levels. The mechanism is downregulation of aquaporin two water channels in the collecting duct after lithium accumulates in the principal cell, so the kidney cannot concentrate urine even when antidiuretic hormone is abundant. Patients compensate by drinking, and the danger arises when illness, surgery or anything else interrupts access to fluid and the sodium climbs quickly. Separate from this, lithium causes a chronic interstitial nephropathy with a slow fall in glomerular filtration rate, so renal function is monitored at least six monthly. Early recognition matters because the concentrating defect is partly reversible if lithium is stopped within a few years but often permanent after prolonged exposure.
key_points: Polyuria at a therapeutic lithium level is a concentrating defect, not toxicity
Dilute urine that stays dilute during water deprivation separates it from primary polydipsia
Amiloride blocks the channel through which lithium enters the principal cell
Never fluid restrict a patient whose thirst is holding the sodium down
Monitor renal function and thyroid function at least every six months on long term lithium
explanation.pearls: Amiloride 5 to 10 mg daily reduces urine volume in lithium induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus within about two weeks, and because it also reduces lithium clearance the serum lithium must be rechecked five to seven days after starting it.

options.rationale: Lithium enters the principal cell through the epithelial sodium channel and disables the collecting duct response to antidiuretic hormone, and amiloride blocks that entry channel and is the specific agent for the resulting concentrating defect. Reviewing the indication runs in parallel because the defect becomes less reversible the longer lithium continues. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Desmopressin replaces antidiuretic hormone and only works when the deficiency is at the pituitary end, whereas here the hormone is present and the collecting duct cannot respond to it. That resistance is precisely what separates the nephrogenic form from the central form that desmopressin treats. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

Her thirst is the compensation that is keeping her sodium at 148 rather than far higher, so capping intake while the renal losses continue risks driving a dangerous hypernatraemia. Fluid restriction is the treatment for primary polydipsia, which the dilute urine and rising sodium during supervised deprivation have already excluded. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Polyuria with thirst does warrant excluding an osmotic diuresis, but a random glucose of 5.2 mmol/L alongside urine that is dilute rather than loaded with solute has already done that. An osmotic cause would produce a urine osmolality well above the serum value rather than the 178 mOsm/kg recorded. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Abrupt lithium withdrawal carries a well described rebound risk of mania over the following months in a woman who has been stable for eight years, so any change is made as a slow taper with a planned alternative. Valproate is also a poor default choice in a woman of reproductive age given its teratogenicity. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: Gambling disorder sits with the substance use disorders in current classification because it shares the features of tolerance, withdrawal, preoccupation and continued use despite harm. It is rarely the presenting complaint, and most people reach a doctor through insomnia, low mood, relationship breakdown or a request for a medical certificate, so a single screening question about betting belongs in any assessment of unexplained distress in this age group. Suicide risk is markedly elevated in gambling disorder, particularly around the point of disclosure to a partner or a creditor, so risk assessment is repeated rather than done once. Australian services combine psychological therapy with free financial counselling and with self exclusion registers that cover venues and online platforms. Comorbid depression, alcohol use and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder are common and are reassessed after the gambling is being treated.
key_points: Ask directly about gambling when insomnia or low mood has no clear explanation
Cognitive behavioural therapy targeting chasing and chance beliefs is first line
Financial counselling and self exclusion support treatment but do not replace it
Suicide risk peaks around disclosure of debt and needs repeated assessment
Reassess mood after the gambling is addressed before diagnosing a depressive disorder
explanation.pearls: Chasing losses, the act of betting more to recover what was lost, is the single most specific feature of gambling disorder and appears earlier than the financial consequences that eventually bring people to a doctor.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Structured cognitive behavioural therapy addressing the erroneous beliefs about chance, the chasing behaviour and cue exposure has the strongest evidence in gambling disorder and is the recommended first treatment. Directing therapy at the gambling rather than at the mood symptom treats the disorder that is generating both. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

His low mood and early morning waking are plausibly secondary to mounting debt and concealment rather than an independent depressive episode, and antidepressants have not shown benefit for gambling disorder itself. This would be the right move if depressive symptoms persisted once the gambling was being treated. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Opioid antagonists have modest evidence in gambling disorder and are considered when psychological treatment has been tried and failed, particularly where there is a strong urge component or a family history of alcohol use disorder. It is a second line addition rather than an opening move. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Financial counselling is a genuinely useful part of the package and Australian gambling help services provide it, but on its own it manages the consequence and leaves the behaviour that created it untouched. It belongs alongside psychological treatment, not instead of it. (Source: Gambling Help Online Australia)

Self exclusion and app blocking reduce access and are worth arranging, but he has already tried deleting the app three times, which shows that removing the means alone has not held. A three month gap also leaves a man with escalating secret debt unsupported. (Source: Gambling Help Online Australia)

explanation.summary: Selective mutism is an anxiety disorder in which a child who speaks normally in comfortable settings is consistently unable to speak in specific social situations, most often school, for at least a month beyond the first month of enrolment. The child is not choosing silence, and framing it to families and teachers as a freeze response rather than defiance changes how the adults around the child behave. Around a third of affected children also meet criteria for social anxiety disorder, and the rate of comorbid anxiety in parents is high. The practical risk of delay is that schools adapt by allowing written or non-verbal responses, which relieves anxiety in the short term and reinforces avoidance over the long term. Prognosis with an early behavioural program is good, and most children gain functional classroom speech.
key_points: Normal speech in one setting excludes a language disorder as the explanation
Duration must exceed one month beyond the initial month of starting school
Treatment is graded exposure delivered in the setting where speech fails
Pressing a child to speak in the moment reliably increases the freeze
Medication follows an inadequate response to behavioural treatment
explanation.pearls: Stimulus fading, in which a parent the child already speaks to is gradually joined in the room by the teacher before the parent withdraws, is the highest yield single technique and is usually where a school program begins.

sources.label: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline

options.rationale: Selective mutism responds to a behavioural program that builds speech through a planned ladder of steps, moving from non-verbal to whispered to spoken responses across widening settings, and it must be run where the mutism occurs rather than only in a clinic room. Involving the teacher is what converts a clinic gain into classroom speech. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline

options.rationale: The recording of fluent conversational speech and singing at home establishes that expressive language is intact, which is the finding that separates selective mutism from a language disorder. Speech pathology has a role only where an additional articulation or language problem is suspected on top of the mutism. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline

options.rationale: Reciprocal play, spontaneous showing, normal eye contact and the absence of repetitive behaviours or restricted interests argue against autism, and the mutism here is situation bound rather than a pervasive social communication difficulty. Autism assessment would be warranted if the social differences were present at home as well. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline

options.rationale: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are reserved for children whose mutism persists despite an adequate behavioural program or who are too anxious to engage with one, so they follow rather than replace therapy. Starting a drug first in a 6-year-old commits her to medication without testing the treatment most likely to work. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

A month or so of silence in a new setting can be normal adjustment, but fourteen months is well beyond that and the longer the mutism is established the harder it becomes to shift. Waiting also allows the school to accommodate around her silence in ways that entrench it. (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline)
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline

explanation.summary: Body dysmorphic disorder is a preoccupation with a perceived defect that is unobservable or slight to others, combined with repetitive behaviours such as mirror checking, comparing, camouflaging or reassurance seeking. It typically begins in adolescence and is under recognised because patients present to dermatologists and surgeons rather than to mental health services. The nose, skin and hair are the most commonly targeted areas, and muscle dysmorphia is a recognised variant in young men. Suicidal ideation and attempts are substantially more frequent than in obsessive compulsive disorder, so risk assessment is part of every review. Insight is often poor and up to a third of patients hold the belief with delusional intensity, which changes neither the diagnosis nor the first line treatment.
key_points: The defect is absent or slight to an observer while the distress is severe
Repetitive checking, comparing or camouflaging is required for the diagnosis
Cosmetic procedures usually leave the preoccupation unchanged or worse
Cognitive behavioural therapy with response prevention is first line
Suicide risk is high and is assessed at every contact
explanation.pearls: Serotonin reuptake inhibitors for body dysmorphic disorder need obsessive compulsive range doses, for example fluoxetine 40 to 80 mg daily, and a twelve week trial before the response is judged, which is longer and higher than the usual depression trial.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: Cosmetic surgery in this setting rarely satisfies the patient and the preoccupation typically transfers to the operated site or to a new body part, with worsening distress afterwards. Surgery would only be appropriate if there were an objective deformity, which examination has excluded. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Poor insight is common in this disorder and does not by itself make the belief delusional or make an antipsychotic the right treatment, since these patients respond to the same therapy as those with better insight. An antipsychotic is considered only as augmentation when a serotonergic drug and therapy have failed. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Cognitive behavioural therapy incorporating exposure to avoided situations and prevention of mirror checking and reassurance seeking is the recommended first treatment and targets the maintaining behaviours directly. Perceptual retraining in front of a mirror is a specific component that ordinary anxiety focused therapy does not include. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Reassurance is itself one of the behaviours that maintains the disorder, giving brief relief followed by renewed doubt and more checking, so repeating it in the consulting room strengthens the cycle. He has already told you that family reassurance does not hold. (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists)
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.rationale: A serotonin reuptake inhibitor at the higher doses used for obsessive compulsive spectrum disorders is an effective treatment and is combined with therapy in moderate to severe illness, but it is not preferred over therapy as the sole opening move. This would be the right answer if therapy were unavailable or he declined it. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

explanation.summary: Shift work disorder is diagnosed when insomnia or excessive sleepiness is temporally linked to a work schedule that overlaps the usual sleep period, persists for at least three months, and is not better explained by another sleep disorder. The discriminating history is that sleep normalises on leave or on a run of day shifts, which separates a circadian misalignment from a primary insomnia. Around a fifth to a quarter of shift workers meet criteria, and night shift, early morning starts and rapidly rotating rosters carry the highest risk. Drowsy driving on the commute home is the most immediate danger and should be asked about explicitly, along with an offer of alternative transport arrangements. Longer term associations include cardiometabolic disease and mood disorder, which is why roster design is part of management rather than an aside.
key_points: Sleep that normalises on annual leave points to a circadian rather than intrinsic disorder
Ask directly about drowsy driving on the commute home
Bright light early in the shift and dark glasses afterwards shift the clock in the wanted direction
Protect the daytime sleep period with darkness, quiet and a silenced phone
Hypnotics and wake promoting drugs follow rather than replace circadian measures
explanation.pearls: A planned nap of 20 to 30 minutes taken before the night shift, or in the first half of it, improves alertness without the deep sleep inertia that follows a nap longer than about 45 minutes.

options.rationale: A hypnotic may lengthen the daytime sleep a little but does nothing for the sleepiness on shift, which is the part that is putting her at risk on the road, and tolerance and dependence follow regular use. Sedatives are a short term adjunct at most, not the opening move. (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook)

A sleep study is indicated when obstructive sleep apnoea, narcolepsy or a periodic limb movement disorder is suspected, and a body mass index of 22 with no snoring, no witnessed apnoea and no limb movements makes those unlikely. The normal sleep on annual leave points firmly to a circadian rather than an intrinsic sleep disorder. (Source: Sleep Health Foundation Australia)
